excluded.reason: Already extracted from its approved high-resolution source as main_hall_retained_shell_throne.png with separate ownership provenance; re-extraction would create duplicate ownership.
The painted side openings are architectural recesses partly occluded by the auditorium rails, not separable door objects; animating them would carry rail or wall fragments.
The large shell is integrated into the stair architecture and overlaps the self-contained foreground bubble fountain; separating both would split or duplicate the same painted pixels.

The small clam is integrated into the giant-clam stair composition; its generated hidden-state trial drifted into a new jar and would have repeated the rejected static-fixture-plus-overlay pattern. Existing Pool objects are upgraded directly instead.
The painted teapot touches the cup, coral, and counter shadow at its spout and handle; repeated masks retained neighboring pixels, so it is rejected instead of shipping a dirty cutout.

Three source-mask refinements could not isolate the knob and lid rim without retaining purple wall pixels or stealing pot-body and right-handle pixels. The candidate is rejected so no baked pot part vanishes during interaction.

The right rack's lowest ribbons overlap the painted wall shelf and cup; exact separation left detached wall fragments, so the existing clean left ribbon interaction remains the room's ribbon activity.

The paper cylinder is painted through its gold holder and overlapping purple plant/wall shadow; removing those pixels cuts an obvious hole in the roll, so it is rejected rather than shipped as a compromised partial cutout.
